_about: The game's own notices in the chat and the message log, set apart from what people say: what's happening where and when. `every` is the range of real seconds between notices while you play. `dawn` and `dusk` play when the calendar's hour turns 6 or 18 (an in-game hour is a real minute). `arrival` plays when you come to a map (by map id), and `bossNearby` when it has a boss you've never beaten ({boss}, {map}). `community` tells what other adventurers have been up to: {bot} is one of them (tagged BOT), {level} a level, {boss} a boss and {rare} a rare monster, {map} where (the boss's or the rare's map), {item} a weapon. A `sighting` really does make a map's rare monster turn up `boost` times as often there for `minutes` real minutes ({monster}, {map}, {minutes}), favouring maps near your level; `chance` is how often a notice is one.
dawn: Dawn breaks over Avalune. Good morning, adventurers!
The sun is up over Avalune. A fine day for an adventure!
Morning comes to Avalune, and the shops open their shutters.
dusk: Night falls over Avalune. Sweet dreams, or happy hunting!
The sun sets over Avalune, and the lamps come on in town.
Evening comes to Avalune. The moon is out!

goldburg: Ingothold's market is open! Traders fill the main square: walk up to one to see what they're selling.
meadowbrook: Welcome to Meadowbrook! New adventurers find their guild masters here.
rainbow_city: Prismhaven is bustling today. Adventurers from all over meet in its streets.
bluebird: Larkspur's streets are full of adventurers today.

bossNearby: Word is {boss} lurks somewhere in {map}. Be ready!

sighting.text: A rare {monster} has been sighted in {map}! For the next {minutes} minutes it turns up there far more often.
sighting.end: The rare {monster} in {map} has gone back into hiding.
